Proposition
[Farther necks have almost larger radii] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0089 ↗ lem:chow-iii-busemann-level-diameter-neck ↗ lem:chow-iii-busemann-attains-minimum 1. ch18:18.33\group Necks and Busemann Functions

There is $\varepsilon (n)>0$ such that the following holds. Let $(\mathcal N^n,h)$ be complete, noncompact, and positively curved, let $\gamma $ be a ray, and let $\mathfrak N_1,\mathfrak N_2$ be disjoint embedded $\varepsilon (n)$-necks with center points $y_1,y_2$. If $d(p_*,y_1)\le d(p_*,y_2)$, where $p_*$ minimizes $b_\gamma $, then \[ R(y_2)\le 144R(y_1). \]
Proof

\sketch The neck separation inequalities give $b_\gamma (y_1)<b_\gamma (y_2)$. Sharafutdinov monotonicity for the convex Busemann function then gives $\operatorname {diam}b_\gamma ^{-1}(b_\gamma (y_1))\le \operatorname {diam}b_\gamma ^{-1}(b_\gamma (y_2))$. Applying the lower and upper diameter bounds of Lemma 4 at $y_1$ and $y_2$, respectively, gives $(11/12)\pi c_nR(y_1)^{-1/2}\le 11\pi c_nR(y_2)^{-1/2}$, which is equivalent to the assertion.

□
